title: Netflix's Minimum Wage Tests the 15-Minute Sitcom
excerpt:
The comedy's first batch features 14 episodes running roughly 12 to 20 minutes.
Its creators see short-form storytelling as a possible streaming direction.
body_md:
Netflix's Minimum Wage is testing whether a traditional sitcom can thrive in a considerably shorter format. Its first group of 14 episodes runs approximately 12 to 20 minutes each, contrasting with the longer episode lengths that have become common in streaming television.

Set inside a pizza restaurant, the comedy grew from short online sketches into a scripted series. Creators Jeremy Garelick and Will Phelps said Netflix encouraged them to embrace compact episodes, prompting changes to their writing process and leaving more room for improvisation by the cast.

The producers believe tightly edited, approximately 15-minute installments could appeal to audiences accustomed to fast-paced digital entertainment. That remains their view of the medium's potential, not an announced requirement for future Netflix programming.
